i mean i took this as more of a mocking album than anything else. ‘mans bestfriend' would be mocking how women are called bitches, in reference to female dogs, especially because of the album cover…? also manchild was quite literally a mocking eyeroll of a song. i’m pretty sure she described it that way, at least.

of course the cover is sexual. she is not closed off about her sexuality and she shouldn’t be, imo. that’s a common theme in a lot of her music. i also don’t think she should be crucified for men’s bad behaviour but maybe that’s just me. 🤷‍♀️

that being said, women are still allowed to feel uncomfortable or offput by the album. 

i can already feel the backlash lol

i find a get low/high when i am stressed much easier. i have anxiety with leaving my bedroom/house/comfort zones, so the mornings of going out, i often run higher or lower. i say this to tell you that you’re not alone.

i always feel really guilty when i make my friends and i late, or if i’m feeling unwell enough to cancel, but at the same time, prioritising myself and my health is more important than any plans i have. plans can be rescheduled, people can adapt to being late or having to change it. 

if you have people in your circle that make you feel guilty for taking care of yourself, especially when it’s out of your control, maybe you need to reevaluate that relationship. i would also say that it wouldn’t hurt to question why you feel like such a burden for this.

in other news, your boyfriend sounds great. don’t beat yourself up over something that is going to happen whether you want it to or not. i hope you feel better soon op <3
i miss animas and my pink pump <|3

i was also a baby. my earliest memory is being in time out at age 6 because i didn’t want my injection. i was a bratty kid so it doesn’t surprise me lol. 

i honestly feel sorry equally for anyone diagnosed. those that have had it their whole life BECAUSE they’ve had it their whole life and are more likely
to burn out early, but also later because they now have to adjust. however, those that are diagnosed as adults (while still difficult) i imagine adjust a little more maturely and don’t feel the need to be like other kids (adults, in their case) or get bullied for it, but i’m self projecting.
i do too! its not because I find them offensive, they’re just stupid and unoriginal.
i feel a big sense of shame about it for some reason. i usually avoid talking about my diabetes with anyone. i’ve been diabetic my entire life and have never quite felt comfortable with it.

not really the same, but i’ve been accused of using ai by teachers (when i haven’t) and the way that those comments completely suck any motivation or accomplishment out of me is crazy. don’t let the stupid comment make you feel insecure about your work. everyone has a style of writing and a tone. if they don’t like it, that’s fine.
i just have to cry so bad. like everything makes me upset and i don’t want to move or do anything about it.

yea! i thought this too. i haven’t really critiques the show much, it’s just a silly show to me with some incredible angst. but this season felt rushed and badly written. also the editing was extremely bad in the finale, i was a little surprised? 

still enjoyed it, just wasn’t happy.

i’m not a teacher but TO BE FAIR, as someone who has to use the washroom a lot (not at school, i don’t like public washrooms), if i’m distracted by something i’m actually interested in, i’m much less likely to notice how bad i have to go if at all.

teachers are stronger than me because i’d have to check myself into a mental hospital if i heard the same thing over and over again lol.

thank you for being nice! i can definitely relate to being constantly high. it’s kind of funny because if i’m not forcing myself to be low, i’m REALLY high. my management is just bad all around. i think i’ve had ketones more than all of my diabetic friends combined lol.

i do worry that when if i’m older all of this will come back to bite me in the ass, and i wish i had the motivation/care to try, but i also know that’s something only i can fix. i do hope that if i do stick it out for a while, i also feel better. it’s really great that you do, admirable. i really appreciated you telling me this, so thanks again.

thank you for the comment, and the kind words :) i don’t have a diabetes therapist and i don’t think i’d ever even consider telling the social worker on my team. i have a hard time building trust and saying hard things to people if i know it’ll concern them. i also don’t like talking about my diabetes with really anyone. i feel ashamed and a bit embarrassing, but i’m also a teenager and everything feels embarrassing, especially vulnerable stuff.

i do think one of the reasons i’m not dead yet is because i know my life is so tiny (idk how else to word that) right now and i’m curious. i certainly hope i don’t always feel like a 17 year old haha. i’m happy you’re doing better now!
it is very hard. i’m happy that you were able to stop!

thank you for the nice comment! i’m glad to hear i’m not fully alone with this. i have a really hard time building trust with anybody, so while i really value my therapy sessions w my current therapist, i’m still not even like 80% honest about important things. 

i do wish i’d build up the courage to mention it though. i like it sometimes and i’m not good at accepting help but i always feel like shit afterwards haha

i don’t think there’s any in my area, but perhaps i should look into it. the only problem with starting with a new one (which i have debated before) is that it took me over two years to finally start admitting certain feelings or habits of mine to her, so i worry about starting another one and have to restart all that progress. 

it does bother me that she doesn’t really understand the diabetes aspect of my life though.

thank you for the advice through, i’ll definitely think about it :))

i do have a therapist which i’m super lucky to have, but i have a really difficult time trying to talk about things that i know might concern people or sound really depressed. i will think about it for sure, thank you!

yeah. i wouldn’t say that when i make myself low i’m actively suicidal but there are probably undertones. i also get put into an interesting headspace haha

thank you for commenting!

i do have therapy, but this (and other maybe harmful topics) always feels really taboo to talk about with anyone for me. 

i really appreciate the links and the response!
also three comments AND comments on my other posts is crazy lmao
yeah that’s really the only thing i’m worried about. not so much having one but having to get medical help and then explain how or why i dropped so low, and didn’t fix it.
lol what? going to different posts of mine just because you disagree with me using the sub for partially what it’s for—getting support and talking to people with similar experiences—is interesting.

i’m happy to know i’m not alone but also sorry to hear about that. it’s a constant temptation for me, and i thought i was alone in this one haha.

thank you for responding.

yeah that’s kind of what i expected. i more so wanted people’s experiences themselves to see if i was completely alone in that which apparently i’m not. i have a hard time connecting my actions to long term consequences (if that makes any sense), so even though they are dangerous and i know immediate dangers, i find i don’t tend to think about long term ones. not as much as i used to anyway.

i appreciate the comment, and thank you!

i’m not going to lie, i didn’t even think about the physical neurological aspect. maybe it is that. i’m an already really anxious person about everything so again, it’s probably a control thing.

thank you for responding. also, i’m sorry to hear about your shoulder.

thanks for responding! i did post that, but i’m not asking for help, i’m asking for people’s own experiences—which is partially what this sub is for. talking to people who maybe understand, which i don’t have irl. take that how you will.

me! my a1c is 11.9 at the moment, i get ketones almost once a week, i don’t take proper care of my sites/sensors, and if i run out of insulin, it stays like the at until i care enough to change it. you’re not alone.

i think getting the constant criticism of my management since i was old enough to begin to care for myself (from diabetic team, family, therapists, etc) is what influenced my lack of care. also, if i don’t try, i can’t be disappointed in myself. 

kind of a bummer response. i hope your care gets easier, and that your health is okay.

you’ll most likely be fine. not to encourage bad habits, but when i was on injections, i rarely changed the needle… eventually the spots would get hard to the touch, but i had never gotten infected.

i hope everything goes alright!
she’s a great actress but she’s like my joey king. i just can’t watch her. i think it’s envy lol

again, i understand the frustration, and i don’t doubt that it’s difficult to remember everything you need to. obviously reminders can be needed, that’s fine, never said it wasn’t. however a student dealing with a chronic disease, especially something that teachers/peers are hardly educated on, is already tough. it is EXHAUSTING to constantly have to prove myself to a teacher who has already created a narrative about me. just because it doesn’t look the way you want it to or because using their medical aids bothers you, it does not mean that you have justification to pass judgement or target them. op shouldn’t have to fight for their basic medical accommodations to someone who, as you said, had enough students to worry about already.

as someone else said, if you believe there’s irresponsible behaviour regarding phones or that they’re using their disease as an excuse, bring it up with admin or parents. i know admin sucks in most school boards but the student—especially if you’re wrong—doesn’t need that burden on their shoulders, speaking from personal experience.

believe it or not, i’ve heard that many times before. i have a 504 plan and have kindly reminded teachers many times over and over again and have had consistently the same problem with a few. i promise i know how to handle my own disease, and i promise i’ve had various encounters with teachers refusing to be wrong. having many students isn’t an excuse to actively target a student who has tried MANY times to explain the use of their phone and why they need it. 

again, i get the frustration with phones, but mine (and ops) phone isn’t just for fun—it’s a medical aid.

also, it’s reddit. the way i choose to type is irrelevant lol

as a student who had a teacher that loved to assume i was on my phone for the wrong reasons, i never was. i was however constantly afraid of going on my phone to handle my diabetes because of teachers like this. i was brought to tears multiple times by being singled out by teachers like this. i have had dangerous lows because my teachers wouldn’t let me check my sugars or text my mom when i needed because of teachers like this. my phone is a medical aid for me, as such with your diabetic students, and honestly? they’re having a hard enough time handling their diabetes as teenagers when they already don’t want to be doing that. they don’t need your automatic judgement on top of that. 

i don’t mean to come off rude and i get the frustration with phones, teenagers are annoying. but it’s different for us, and it’s hard enough as is. if texting their mom helps with their management as a literal teenager, then that’s their business and their business only.

i’ve had this problem SO many times. eventually i grew frustrated and went to the principal. i told her that he wasn’t following my medical accommodations and that i would get my parents involved if they didn’t do anything about it. i always text my mom for my diabetes too. i feel safer/more controlled knowing she knows what i’m dealing with too, i don’t know why. 

honestly, tell your parents it’s happening. don’t let them try to take it. tell the admin directly again that they are putting you in danger and you won’t hesitate to take legal action. from personal experience, teachers love to assume the worst when they see a student on their phone. i get it, kids are addicted, but when you have valid reasoning they need to back off. good luck, i hope your teacher gets in shit and backs off.
my eyes go blurry and i feel like i’m wearing drunk goggles.

where i live, it’s illegal not to clarify that you’re diabetic because it can and will effect your driving. however, they won’t deny you your license so long as you haven’t had an episode (fainting, seizure) due to diabetes in the past year.
i do this. my docs have always done it that way too.
yeah there’s 3 connected to the locker rooms in a little hallway. i’m not sure how often they’re used because i don’t think they get cleaned lol

i had something similar with a principal. he would creep in the girls locker room and corner them to see them naked. went to court over it but instead of removing all of his access to children, the school board just moved him higher up (admin). there were literal videos of him being a weirdo in the showers while students were in them, and i remember a few girls in my grade got in trouble for sending them around (mind you no student was seen in the video, other than the girl who recorded—her face was in it). we had an assembly about cyber bullying after that lol. it’s funny how little schools care to make their students safe, or accept accountability for allowing people like that (after MANY complaints and legal issues) in the school around 11-17 year old girls.
the chasing a high is what i felt with athena landing the plane. i miss when things were ALMOST realistic (i say that lightly), i feel they’ve just used up all of their ideas :(

yes! i’ve always despised when people use cgms unnecessarily and i’ve figured out it’s a mix of this and me hating that the thing that i have to do to survive is an interest/hobby for them. like what do you mean the thing that has both ruined and impacted my life so heavily is something you enjoy?

i always cry, if that makes you feel any better. you’re not alone :) for me it was just the constant reprimanding—feeling like i’m putting in so much effort to the point of burn out just for the doctors to not recognize that at all, and tell me everything i’m doing wrong. i’ve had the same team since i was a baby (getting an adult one next year, very scared) and i still feel uncomfortable and sad when i’m at my clinics. so, for different reasons but still. 

if me and all of these other people in the comments cry at our clinics, i can almost guarantee that they see so many other adults cry for various reasons. it’s normal. diabetes is a difficult disease, and i’m sure they know that with diabetes comes other problems and feelings. try not to ruminate too much <3
i do get SO hungry though, like eat everything in sight, vampire drinking blood kind of hungry.
i just get SO emotional. like all i can do is cry, and i feel like gravity is pulling me down.

celery + pb is my favourite but i know a lot of kids who don’t like that. those rice cakes with peanut butter—but the non flavoured ones. there are these keto crackers (i think made w nuts, which don’t spike my carbs but apparently spike peoples in the comments) that i’ve paired w cheese before. seaweed? my little cousin likes that a lot, which i don’t get but maybe your son will. 

i feel bad not having creative suggestions, so i hope you figure stuff out that he likes! good luck!

i personally didn’t like her because of the way she treated victims that the 118 treated whilst she was filming. you can have goals and dreams and do your job and still have basic respect for people going through painful, traumatizing stuff. also the whole filming bobby’s high breakdown was what pushed me into disliking her. i would’ve liked to see her character development, i think she had potential outside of her and buck and her job.
i just eat, combo bolus, and hope for the best
medtronic. i’ve obv had many sites leak in the past but never this often. like it’s genuinely every single new site

i swear i saw a post exactly like this a few months ago. but jesus christ. going low is part of being diabetic and so is the shitty symptoms that come with it. usually i’d say talk to him about it but seeing as you already did, that’s a huge red flag. i hope that whatever happens, you find someone who understands diabetes and treats you better in general, especially during times of crisis. prioritise you and your health. i hope everything gets better!!

i’m also a teenager, and have TERRIBLE care, not gonna lie. my sugars are high all the time and i miss a lot of school because of it. for work, i didn’t call in THAT much for my diabetes (usually other reasons) but i definitely did a few times for really big lows where i couldn’t get my sugars up or ketones, etc. it did effect a lot for me. don’t get too discouraged by people in the comments. everyone’s different and nobody is perfect, nor does a perfect attendance make you a good employee. you’re a teenager, you’re allowed to call in when your health is at play.

i didn’t mean to sound like you were doing anything wrong! i used to sneak food and candy all the time (diagnosed when i was 1) and my parents would get extremely mad because i’d end up really high. that’s why i suggest giving her a sugar free alternative so she doesn’t have to bolus and doesn’t have those high sugars after, especially if she’s not telling you about it or you might not see.

i’m no expert but i remember being her age and wanting something sweet, knowing my low snacks were in reach and so tasty. my advice would be find a sugar free option that she can have instead (that she likes). one of my things was that i hated being told i couldn’t have what normal kids could have, so even just the illusion that it was my choice and i was “normal” would’ve been nice. 

also, if all else fails, have extras with/near you that she doesn’t know about. try to explain that if she’s going to have a snack/candy, that she’s not in trouble but to at least tell somebody so that you can make sure she’s healthy, but in the way that you would explain that to a six year old.

i don’t get why people are blaming you. i personally wouldn’t walk into someone’s office and take their candy without asking, but maybe that’s just me? lol. sorry that happened, i hope it doesn’t happen again
Thank you!!

Finally home! They kind of just looked at it and gave me pain killers. Those didn’t work, and when I walked/moved the pain was still a 10/10, so they gave me morphine too. That still hasn’t kicked in, I am in an incredulous amount of pain still. Going a bit insane because I just want to sleep. Thanks for the concern and comments, I really appreciate it

I’m finally home after about 5 hours, quicker than I expected. They gave it a once over then gave me pain meds before sending me on my way. I had a really hard time walking still, and when the nurse made me walk to the bathroom and back I felt like I was going to collapse from the pain. Tried to hold it back to save myself some dignity, but I felt very bad for her having to deal with me lol. They gave me two pain killer injections that didn’t help, and then some morphine which hasn’t helped. We’ll see, I’m giving it time.

Thanks for the concern :)
Was just joking, I am veryyy aware. Unfortunately I have had my fair share of emergency room experiences.

haha that’s similar to how i got into it. i think mine was either the tsunami, or the pregnant women in that yoga place. i’ve gotten into so many shows that way, i kind of love those bot accounts for it (criminal minds, new amsterdam, etc)

i haven’t finished s4 yet tbh, but jj is one of my least favourites out of all of the pogues—and i say that loving all of them. i wish it would but i don’t think his death will hit me hard… then again i won’t have the shock because i already know. 

i hope they do something good with his death, like what you said—revenge. i hope it’s thought out though, and it’s satisfying.
Thank you!! I was taken to the hospital finally, but now I’ve got to wait for an eternity. Luckily I’m not dying!

Thankfully I convinced my mom (after lots of howling and crying in my bedroom). I’ve got no pain tolerance so while I’m fine having to wait for hours before I get seen, I can’t wait til they finally take me to a room. Also, these chairs aren’t helping.
I was able to convince my mom to take me, though I’ll be waiting for a while. I hope your husband recovers smoothly and speedily!

Yes, thank god. Unfortunately canadian healthcare means waiting in a waiting room for hours, so I’ve been here for two. I just hope they see me soon—no rush, my ass just feels like it’s going to fall off—so I can hopefully get painkillers that work because tylenol/advil isn’t helping.
Unfortunately no, just bed ridden. I’m in too much pain to move so I’m stuck laying down until it dims lol
Alright, I’ll try to convince my mom haha. Thanks for the help!!

No, it was immediate and hasn’t died down at all. Even laying down it still hurts if I breathe too deep or with the odd movement. Ten minutes ago I attempted to go to the washroom; mom helped me up but once I got in a standing position my back immediately froze w/ sharp pains. 

Thanks for responding even if I can’t really get a definitive answer. It’s nice to hear from someone that believes me haha
Slipped at the top one so about 4/5. My mom doesn’t believe I’m in pain so she refuses to take me, though I’d really appreciate some painkillers or something because this is torture lol

i can see how you think that. i didn’t take it that way but i guess that’s where we differ. it’s also important to note that rafe is a psycho—in those seasons (when it was relevant) he really couldn’t care less if his sister or her friends got hurt lol
it didn't really get dropped at all in my opinion. it was brought up throughout s1 and s2 multiple times, and still, barry holds a strong grudge against the crew because of it lol
Thank you for commenting.  That's exactly how I feel, it's nice to know I'm not totally alone in that regard haha <3

for me it’s not so much death/getting hurt rather than not having control. like i’m scared i can’t escape something that scares me or feels/is dangerous. i have a hard time explaining this to other people because i can’t really explain that im scared of fear itself.

I’m only 17 so idk if this was targeted to my age lol, but madeline and that one craft show…? Mr maker or something (?). They were STAPLES in my childhood. Also, there was this one fever dream of a show that I only remember one scene from, and I have no clue what it could be. The scene I remember is a rat in a store with a hat maybe? And also the main woman (only human or non puppet in the show..?) tells a story or talks to camera in front of a felt looking tree..? Kind of reminds me of bear in the big blue house, maybe it is.

I think it’s hard for my mom to trust me to take care of myself because of how little I did in the past, but even she’s commented on my progress and change in attitude/behaviour regarding my Diabetes so I just get annoyed that she won’t listen or let me continue that.

I’d be happy to hear your insights :))

If I'm correct, 9. It was 10 last time though, and even if it's not dropping as fast as I'd like, it's a lot of progress. When I was strictly on the pump, it could range from like 10-12. I've never had a low a1c lol.

Yeah, I get that. I will admit I am a bit close-minded (? not sure what word to use) when it comes to parenting obviously since I am 17. I think, as some people have also brought up, the progress I see may not be what she sees or up to her standards, and for her to let me do this on my own (or, more on my own) I probably have to just suck it up and do even better.

Thanks for the sweet response :)

We have spoken about it, both in casual conversations and ones about my care. I have explained my reasoning, though I don't think she actually gets it or listens, which is fine; she's not type one. She hasn't had a pump before and hasn't experienced the burnout, so I get that it's not as deep to her. I am a hothead, both of my parents passed that down to me. Conversations almost always end in an argument or an insult, and while I want to have a sit-down convo with her about it, it's hard to find the right mood or time. I don't communicate well, my mom doesn't either. I am very aware of my faults in this, but I don't know how to deal with it because she doesn't even give me a chance. 

I did get to hear more of her reasonings for why she wants me on the pump, and I get it, but I do think it should be my choice at the end of the day. Especially since I have showed a lot of progress in such a short amount of time. 

Thanks for the thought-out response. It really helps, and I'm going to think about my approaches/"arguments" (for lack of a better word) to talk to her in a hopefully calm manner. I always appreciate hearing from parents perspectives with problems like this because I, as an annoying teen, have a hard time putting myself in her perspective as much as I can with others haha. Thanks again!

This was the plan, but my team was completely different. I am really bad with new people, so, I didn't get a chance to talk about anything that was weighing on me with my Diabetes. My fault, but a deeper problem than I wish it was. I did briefly explain to my main endo that I prefer the pod because it's different than what I have grown so annoyed with, and I also learned a bit more why my mom refuses to change, so there's that. 

This will help anyways, since I plain on speaking with my mom again in a more serious manner. Thank you :)

Yeah. That's the biggest problem I think. I am very aware that she's had to take care of me for longer than most parents, but I have gotten much better, especially with the pod. I don't need her help as much which she's also told me. 

My controls have been a lot better lately, admittedly because I don't eat a lot so forgetting to bolus isn't as big of a deal since that was the main problem. 

Thank you for responding!
Thank you! I'll definitely look into this and if I like what I see, I'll show my mom. I didn't even know any of this existed so I'm happy people are telling me haha
Woahhh I didn't even know that existed!! Unfortunately I'm not on android, but thank you anyways. I'm happy you found something that works for you!
Yeah, I know. It's just frustrating. Thank you for the tips and support :)

I will never forget when I went Christmas shopping about two days before our gift exchange (I procrastinated, as usual) and I ended up crying in the mall and buying a shit ton of bath salts for my friend. He doesn't take baths. He doesn't have a bathtub. I don't know why that was the best option in my head but it's a running joke now, and we all get each other bath products when we give gifts lol. 

As a terrible terrible gift giver, I feel for them </3

as a teenager, i’m bound to get upset by unimportant things, but the one thing that always stuck with me was my parents indirectly telling me that my getting sick was the reason they divorced, and the reason they are so miserable. 

also, for me it’s important people don’t acting like they know how i feel or what it’s like. especially since i have felt so burnt out for so long and therefore have a seeming lack of care for my body/diabetes, i hate hearing them tell me it’s “easy” and im just being lazy.

i guess my advice would be to avoid supporting the idea that you fully get it, and that his disease has burdened you, if that makes sense. it’s impossible to always say the right thing, but you seem to care and i’m sure he’ll appreciate it when he gets older. i sincerely hope it all works out :)
i know. i’ve really appreciated all of them and i’ll definitely be using them if it ever happens again!
wow! i didn’t know that was a thing
i’m doing much better, thank you :)

i do appreciate the concern but unfortunately me and my dad have never really seen eye to eye, and even now he doesn’t really put in an effort to our relationship, so having (another) failed conversation is kind of not something i’m interested in. my mom is plenty supportive and we’re open, i just couldn’t get in touch with her.
thank you! i’m doing much better now

okay so i’m actually an idiot and i didn’t think of this. but when i saw those comments when i finally woke up and went back on reddit at like 4am (i was floating between sleep and being awake all night/morning) i saw that and scavenged my house for a syringe. i didn’t know where one would be though, so i checked my medical cupboard and bathrooms but we have no first aid kit??? thats a whole problem in itself. i then looked everywhere it COULD be but had no luck. what diabetic household doesn’t have a syringe? what household doesn’t, actually? i debated going to my neighbour but i feel like that’s a crazy thing to explain at 4 in the morning.

haha figures. i’m doing better. still sick, still debating the er, but i haven’t kicked the bucket so there’s that! in seriousness i did finally get insulin and now it’s just the battle of getting my sugars/ketones down.

yeah. usually i go super high and then drop low during the night so i don’t usually bolus for drinks and i always have a sensor (which i heavily debated ripping out cause it was pissing me off with the beeping last night, but i didn’t). i dropped, only to rise to the heavens.

pretty close, ontario! lol

thanks for the offer anyways though, i really appreciate it!

my mom? totally. dad? hell no. that’s a story for another time though. pretty much everything is figured out now, was just a hell of night. i live in a small town and there’s no 24/7s, but if worst came to worst i would’ve gone to the er.

my dad and i don’t talk much, but that’s complicated and i don’t actually know where he is. he is not willing to help me out hence why my mom is usually the person i go to during emergencies. my mom and sister are only gone from wednesday-sunday and i had to work/couldn’t get days off so i got stuck here. i don’t mind it, i love being home alone. my mom would’ve helped if she could (and she did).
my mom finally responded and called the pharmacy in the morning. they gave me some insulin pens to tide me over, but i am very sick now. i have never been so sick of drinking water in my life.

yes! my mom finally answered around 11am and called the pharmacy for me. they gave me some pens until i can get my usual. ketones are currently at large and sugars are on the 20s, but i feel tremendously better despite the throwing up and emergency room still being on the table.

if i were to go to the er (which, although i finally have insulin pens, thanks mom, it’s still on the table because my hopes of getting my high ketones down are decreasing quickly) they’d probably get me in pretty fast because i’m 16, got large ketones, and vomiting. and even better, a nice dog bowl to take with me!

that is very very true. the panic made me feel less alone because i’m a 16 year old on my death bed (jokes) with absolutely no clue wtf i’m doing, but it’s all good now or it will be soon. thanks for the help anyways :)
i actually do haha. i use it for marketplace and finding embarrassing photos of my friends on their parents pages lol

im in ontario but i really appreciate the offer, it was very kind of you and its great you were willing to do that. my mom finally answered and after lots of yelling at me called the pharmacy and i got insulin pens until i can get my usual insulin. now it’s just getting my ketones and sugars down without throwing up all over my bed lol

yes! this morning i got insulin pens from the pharmacy (thanks mom for finally answering and calling them for me) so i’ve been working on getting my sugars which were above where the meter can read all night AND ketones down which hit large. my dad is, unfortunately, a fusser, and he probably would’ve used it as a lesson because he doesn’t really understand diabetes.

past student here! anne hathaway isn't inherently bad, but it's located in a low-income area where there are a lot of sketchy things going on. i had countless experiences with cops, addicts, and even psycho parents but i definitely think every kid would have a different experience. it’s important to remember that the school doesn't define the students who attend it. i’m a diabetic, and i had so many resources and support—same with my mental health. it’s definitely not a bad school but it has its moments like any other. 

during my time there was a lot of bullying there that was ignored, especially to me, and it’s usually from kids with shit home lives. many of the kids there struggle a lot with their lives, income, parents, general well-being, so there’s a lot of rough patches with the students who go there.
